'''Alfred Legoyt''' (1812–1885)<ref name="BrianJaisson2007">{{cite book|author1=Éric Brian|author2=Marie Jaisson|title=The Descent of Human Sex Ratio at Birth: A Dialogue between Mathematics, Biology and Sociology|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HgIomnaL_OAC&pg=PA75|date=24 July 2007|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-1-4020-6036-6|pages=75–}}</ref> was a French statistician who organised the [[Census in France|census of France]] in 1856, 1861 and 1866.<ref name="GreenWeil2007">{{cite book|author1=Nancy L. Green|author2=Francois Weil|title=Citizenship and Those Who Leave: The Politics of Emigration and Expatriation|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Dqawo0Kpvz0C&pg=PA120|date=12 March 2007|publisher=University of Illinois Press|isbn=978-0-252-09141-4|pages=120–}}</ref> With his access to vital statistics Legoyt was the most important official statistician of France and was the official delegate to the [[International Statistical Congress]]es held in different European cities between 1853 and 1876.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Aldrich|first=John|title=Tales of two Societies&nbsp;– London and Paris 1860–1940|journal=Electronic Journal for History of Probability and Statistics|date=December 2010|volume=6|issue=2|pages=4–5|url=http://www.jehps.net/Decembre2010/Aldrich.pdf}}</ref>

==Early career==
Legoyt started his career as a clerk in the [[Ministry of the Interior (France)|Ministry of the Interior]] and went on to be the deputy chief of the ministry's Bureau of Statistics in 1839.<ref name="GreenWeil2007" /> In 1833 the [[INSEE|Statistique Générale de la France]] was created as the division of statistics of the [[Ministry of Commerce (France)|Ministry of Commerce]].<ref name="Desrosières2002">{{cite book|author=Alain Desrosières|title=The Politics of Large Numbers: A History of Statistical Reasoning|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hqO0Qvjy4HsC&pg=PA151|year=2002|publisher=Harvard University Press|isbn=978-0-674-00969-1|pages=151–154}}</ref> Legoyt replaced [[:fr:Alexandre Moreau de Jonnès|Alexandre Moreau De Jonnes]] as director of the Statistique Générale de la France in 1852.<ref name="Cole2000">{{cite book|author=Joshua Cole|title=The Power of Large Numbers: Population, Politics, and Gender in Nineteenth-century France|url=https://archive.org/details/poweroflargenumb00cole|url-access=registration|year=2000|publisher=Cornell University Press|isbn=978-0-8014-3701-4|pages=[https://archive.org/details/poweroflargenumb00cole/page/114 114]–115}}</ref> Unlike Moreau de Jonnès Legoyt placed more importance on the practical work of data collection rather than on classification and analysis.<ref name="Schweber2006">{{cite book|author=Libby Schweber|title=Disciplining Statistics: Demography and Vital Statistics in France and England, 1830–1885|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yp8GHhnXQngC&pg=PA51|date=7 November 2006|publisher=Duke University Press|isbn=978-0-8223-8852-4|pages=51–52}}</ref>

==The 1856 Census==
When Legoyt became director of SGF he took over the responsibility of organising the census from the bureau of statistics of the Ministry of the Interior and placed it under the stewardship of the SGF.<ref name="Desrosières2002" /> As the Census Commissioner, of the forthcoming quinquennial census of 1856 Legoyt instructed his officials to use the households as the basis for the enumeration<ref name="Cole2000" /> and to confine to the recording the occupation of the head of the family. It differed significantly from the 1851 Census in which the profession of all enumerated persons, including family dependents were recorded.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Grantham|first=George|title=Occupation, Marital Status and Life-Cycle Determinants of Women's Labour Force Participation in Mid-nineteenth-Century Rural France|journal=EHES Working Papers in Economic History|date=July 2012|issue=22|page=5|url=http://ehes.org/EHES_No22.pdf}}</ref>  In the words of Legoyt, {{blockquote|... include in each profession not only the head of the family, but also every person directly or indirectly supported by his profession, that is to say, his family, his workers, his various agents, and even his servants.}}

Legoyt held the position of director of SGF until the fall of the [[Second French Empire|Second Empire]] in 1870.<ref name="GreenWeil2007" />

He also served as the first permanent secretary of [[:fr:Société française de statistique|Société de Statistique de Paris]] from its creation in 1861 throughout the Second Empire.<ref name="Schweber2006" />

He received an award from the [[Alliance Israélite Universelle]] for his book, ''De la vitalité de la race juive en Europe'' (1865).<ref>Ariane Chebel d’Appollonia, [[CEVIPOF]] (Sciences-Po) (2005), [http://cems.as.nyu.edu/docs/IO/3812/Ariane.pdf "We Can't Be Antisemitic, We Are All French: History, Legacy and Sustainability of the French Model of Integration"], 18 p.</ref>
